dating.source_chronology: Ussher is retained as source provenance only; none of his dates supplies an adopted interval endpoint.
dating.justification: The fortieth year uses inclusive counting: 1446 minus 39 is 1407. Caleb's forty-five years and ages give circa 1401-1400. Shiloh follows Gilgal without its own exact year; 1399 is the owner-chosen completed-allotment stop. Joshua 13 recalls Moses' earlier grants; no lot is asserted at 1446.
dating.alternative: 1400 uses Caleb's ages as elapsed years; 1401 uses the inclusive forty-five years. Neither reading dates the Shiloh survey exactly. Joshua 19:47 is undated and is recorded separately. No universal shift is applied to other chronology.

relation_readings.primary: Riblah is east of Ain; the border goes to Riblah.
relation_readings.alternative: The east-of-Ain clause qualifies the border approach rather than the named settlement.
relation_readings.justification: The KJV's relative clause follows Riblah. Both attachments preserve Ain as the positional target; neither supplies a Site or Course.

relation_readings.primary: The ascent of Adummim lies south of the unnamed river.
relation_readings.alternative: The south-of-river clause qualifies Gilgal rather than the intervening ascent.
relation_readings.justification: The nearest antecedent in the KJV is the going up to Adummim. The unnamed river remains unlocated; no modern river identification is chosen.

relation_readings.primary: The hill is before and west of Hinnom, at the northern end of the valley of giants.
relation_readings.alternative: Northward describes the border's arrival at the end of the valley rather than naming its northern end.
relation_readings.justification: The KJV relates the hill to both valleys. Joshua 18:16 separately places the mountain in the valley of giants on the north; the two verses' wording is retained without identifying the hill.

relation_readings.primary: Judah upon Jordan is the owner-chosen eastern upper-Jordan boundary reference.
relation_readings.alternative: Keil's Havoth-jair reading, a town named Judah, and the textual witness remain alternatives on the atlas claim.
relation_readings.justification: The owner-chosen reading is retained as a neighbour relation toward the sunrising, never a course to southern Judah or a possession assertion.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And the coast shall go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain; and the border shall descend, and shall reach unto the side of the sea of Chinnereth eastward:
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: Riblah and Ain are separate; the recorded grammatical alternative is Medium.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And their coast was from Aroer, that is on the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain by Medeba;
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: The Arnon bank is the target; the unnamed river city remains separately unlocated.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And from Heshbon unto Ramath–mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim unto the border of Debir;

And the border went up toward Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northward, looking toward Gilgal, that is before the going up to Adummim, which is on the south side of the river: and the border passed toward the waters of En–shemesh, and the goings out thereof were at En–rogel:
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: Gilgal/ascent attachment repaired; F-291 remains because the unnamed river label reverses the recorded primary south-of relation.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And the border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite; the same is Jerusalem: and the border went up to the top of the mountain that lieth before the valley of Hinnom westward, which is at the end of the valley of the giants northward:
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: The hill and its relations to both valleys are explicit; the alternative remains Medium.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And the border went out toward the sea to Michmethah on the north side; and the border went about eastward unto Taanath–shiloh, and passed by it on the east to Janohah;
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: Janohah is the destination; Taanath-shiloh is the east-of target.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: Southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea is his border; and they met together in Asher on the north, and in Issachar on the east.
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: Manasseh is the subject and Asher the northern neighbour; no course inferred.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And was drawn from the north, and went forth to En–shemesh, and went forth toward Geliloth, which is over against the going up of Adummim, and descended to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben,
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: Geliloth is the subject of over-against the ascent of Adummim.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And their coast was from Heleph, from Allon to Zaanannim, and Adami, Nekeb, and Jabneel, unto Lakum; and the outgoings thereof were at Jordan:
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: Adami and Nekeb remain separate textual names despite the shared atlas identity.

kjv_spot_checks.kjv: And Me–jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border before Japho.
kjv_spot_checks.assessment: The border-before-Japho relation retains its subject without a possession claim.
